title: HB83 (2021 Regular): AN ACT relating to firearms and declaring an emergency.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Kentucky); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Kentucky text (Introduced, 0000-00-00; official copy, https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/21RS/hb83/orig_bill.pdf (LegiScan doc 2228662))
provenance.note: Introduced print (no date on the print); no passage vote in the data, so it is the bill as filed. 2021 Regular Session. Section 15 takes effect Jan. 1, 2022; the rest on passage (emergency clause). Section 15 also covers handgun registration, assault weapons and a sales log (not quoted for length). Also adds: estate inventory lists each firearm (KRS 395.250), judge must demand surrender of guns after a not-guilty-by-reason-of-insanity or guilty-but-mentally-ill finding (KRS 504.030, 532.030), facilitation covers supplying a firearm (KRS 506.080), felon-in-possession sentence runs consecutively (KRS 527.040), postsecondary schools added to the school weapons ban (KRS 527.070); conforming changes to KRS 237.104, 237.115, 532.025. Not quoted for length.

operative_text:
Section 2 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) In addition to any other requirement of state or federal law, all sales, exchanges, or transfers of firearms shall be conducted in accordance with this section unless such sale, exchange, or transfer is: (a) Conducted by a licensed importer, licensed manufacturer, or licensed dealer, as those terms are defined in 18 U.S.C. secs. 921 and 922, when such sale, exchange, or transfer is conducted pursuant to that person’s federal firearms license; or (b) Between spouses, children, and stepchildren in the same immediate family. (2) Before any sale, exchange, or transfer pursuant to this section, a national instant criminal background check shall be completed by a dealer who consents to conduct such a check, and upon completion of such a background check, shall complete a document, the form of which shall be developed and distributed by the Department of Kentucky State Police, that identifies and confirms that such a check was performed.
Section 3 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) Any owner or other person lawfully in possession of a firearm who suffers the loss or theft of the firearm or any person who sells ammunition who suffers a loss or theft of ammunition shall within twenty-four (24) hours of the discovery of the loss or theft report the facts and circumstances of the loss or theft to a local police department or sheriff’s office.
Section 4 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) No person who owns or is custodian of a firearm shall store or otherwise leave the firearm out of his or her immediate possession or control without having first securely locked the firearm in an appropriate safe storage depository or rendered it incapable of being fired by use of a gun-locking device appropriate to that weapon, including through the use of a safe or other secure container which, when locked, is incapable of being opened without the key, combination, or other unlocking mechanism and is capable of preventing an unauthorized person from obtaining access to and possession of its contents.
Section 15 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) (a) The Department of Kentucky State Police shall promulgate an administrative regulation for the licensure of persons to possess a handgun in the Commonwealth of Kentucky. The administrative regulation shall prohibit the possession of a handgun by a person in Kentucky unless the person holds such a license or falls within an exemption that the Department of Kentucky State Police may create in the administrative regulation. The license shall be available to persons who are at least twenty-one (21) years old or who have been honorably discharged from the Armed Forces of the United States who meet the eligibility criteria established by the department, and who are not otherwise prohibited by state or federal law from possessing a handgun.
Section 11 (new section of KRS Chapter 527): (1) A person is guilty of criminal purchase or transfer of a weapon when: (a) Knowing that he or she is prohibited by law from possessing a firearm because of a prior conviction or is otherwise ineligible to lawfully possess a firearm under state or federal law, the person purchases a firearm from another person; (b) Knowing that it would be unlawful for another person to possess a firearm, he or she purchases a firearm for, on behalf of, or for the use of that other person; or (c) Knowing that another person is prohibited by law from possessing a firearm because of a prior conviction or is otherwise ineligible to lawfully possess a firearm under state or federal law, a person transfers a firearm to that other person. (2) Criminal purchase or disposal of a weapon is a Class D felony.
Section 12 (KRS 527.040): (c) Sentences for violation of this section shall be served subsequent to the service of any other felony sentence imposed on the offender.
Section 18 (repeal of KRS 65.870): The following KRS section is repealed: 65.870 Local firearms control ordinances prohibited -- Exemption from immunity -- Declaratory and injunctive relief.
